name: Persinger lab: burst-firing through both temporal lobes (20 min)
origin: Laurentian University Behavioural Neuroscience Laboratory (Persinger, Koren, Richards)
summary: The Persinger lab's workhorse exposure: its amygdala-derived 'burst-firing' pattern through both temporal lobes at 1 uT for 20 min, here 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s) once every 4 s because the point values were never published. The lab reported more pleasant narratives with it (Richards 1993) but also more aggression and less trust after three weekly sessions (Gillis 1993), and it stands in for the 'both hemispheres' arm of the lab's suggestibility and sensed-presence studies (Healey 1996; Persinger & Healey 2002).
notes: The papers describe 1-uT (10 mG) fields 'through the temporal planes' or 'along the temporal plane', both sides at once, for 20 min (Gillis 1993; Healey 1996; Persinger & Healey 2002, there 100 nT-1 uT 'equally across both hemispheres' and no named pattern, so burst-firing for that arm is an assumption); Freeman 1996 ran 30 min, and Richards 1993 applied the field only 'briefly' while people told stories. The lab never gave 10-20 positions for its solenoids; two coils per side at T7/TP7 and T8/TP8 (like the four-solenoid 'Koren boxes') are an inference from 'temporal planes' and 'temporoparietal', and the other four channels stay silent. The lab's burst-firing point values were never published; the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz) stands in, with the file's published length, 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s; Carniello 2020; other theses give 248 or 289), once every 4 s (the lab's rat analgesia work, Martin & Persinger 2004, and Collins 2014's Shiva study; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009 give 'once every 3 s for about 0.7 s'). The spacing in the 1990s studies is not published: Gillis & Persinger's comparison arm was a field 'pulsed (1 sec. every 4 sec.)' that did not raise aggression, and their title contrasts 'pulsed vs continuous' fields, so their burst-firing arm may have run without pauses (see persinger-gillis-1993-pulsed-bilateral). The reported effects are single-lab, small-n and not consistent in sign: more aggression and less trust after 3 weekly 20-min sessions (Gillis 1993), better mood and vigour after 3 weekly 20-min sessions of rotated burst-firing (Tsang 2009), irritability when the session was repeatedly interrupted by questions (Freeman 1996). Compare blind with persinger-healey-burst-right, persinger-healey-burst-left and sham (the app's Blind option). Independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop at once on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Blindfolded or with opaque goggles, reclining in a quiet, dark room (the lab used a grounded acoustic chamber of 2.74 x 2.54 x 1.98 m and asked people to notice whatever happens without labelling it).
schedule: One 20-min exposure; Gillis & Persinger gave three, one week apart. At most once a week.
